data.title: Bitcoin ETFs see $21M inflow, easing recent sel... | Pluang
data.description: Bitcoin ETFs experienced a $21.13 million inflow on Friday, led by Blackrock’s IBIT, signaling a pause after two days of heavy redemptions totaling nearly $1 billion. This modest inflow suggests institutional selling pressure on Bitcoin may be easing, though it remains to be seen if this will lead to renewed buying. Meanwhile, Ether ETFs continued to face outflows, losing $56.10 million and extending their streak to nine consecutive days, highlighting a divergence in institutional interest between Bitcoin and Ether. NEAR ETFs attracted fresh capital, contrasting with outflows in Solana ETFs, reflecting selective investor preferences. Overall, Bitcoin's price stability depends on whether new institutional demand can pick up, as current gains are largely driven by existing holders rather than fresh inflows.
data.author: Bitcoin
